title: We describe homes exactly as they are.
lead: Halden & Rowe is a small agency for buying, selling and renting homes in twelve US cities. We started in Brooklyn in 2012 and have kept the team small on purpose.

teamImage.alt: Four colleagues gathered around a table reviewing papers together.

story.headline: Started with a tape measure and a spreadsheet
paragraphs: Clara Halden spent her first years after architecture school drawing other people's homes. Thomas Rowe spent ten years appraising them. They met over a Brooklyn townhouse whose advertised floor area was larger than its plans, and agreed that buyers deserved better information than that.

They opened Halden & Rowe in 2012 with three habits that still shape the agency. We measure every home ourselves. We tell buyers and renters what we know about a home's condition before they visit. And each home has one agent, whose name and number are on the listing, from the first call to the handover of the keys.

values.name: Measured
values.line: Every floor area is one we checked.
values.body: Our agents measure each home before it is listed. If a figure comes from public records or the owner instead, the listing says so.

values.name: Plain
values.line: Fees and terms in writing, before anything is signed.
values.body: Sellers see our fee and what it covers in their agreement. Renters see the deposit, term and pet policy on the listing page.

values.name: Named
values.line: One agent for each home, from first call to keys.
values.body: You deal with the same person throughout. If they are away, they tell you who is covering and for how long.

team.headline: Six agents, one way of working
team.lead: Each agent works in the cities they know, and each one shows their own homes.

detailImage.alt: Ornate stone facade with carved cornice and arched windows catching warm light.

founderQuote: If the floor area and the description are accurate, a viewing is about whether you like the house, not about what we left out.
